notetype.intro: Decide which boxes you fill in when adding a note and which cards a note turns into; the ready-made types are usually enough.
notetype.sort_field_hint: Shown as the note's title in the Library and in search results.
notetype.syntax_intro: Each template makes one card from every note. To put a field on the card, write its code in double braces, e.g. {{word}}.
notetype.pick_desc: Every note belongs to a type. The ready-made types come with the app; for one of your own, use “New note type” and start from a ready-made starting point.
notetype.name_hint: You see this name in the type list when adding a note.
notetype.used_by: {notes, plural, =0 {No notes use this type yet.} one {# note uses this type.} other {# notes use this type.}}
notetype.makes_cards: {cards, plural, =1 {Each note becomes 1 card.} other {Each note becomes up to # cards.}}
notetype.makes_cloze: Every gap you mark in a note becomes its own card.
notetype.fields_desc: The boxes you fill in when adding a note, in this order. A note isn't saved while a required field is empty.

role.none_desc: The app gives this field no special meaning.
role.hint: When you say what each field contains, the app doesn't have to guess which one is the word, the meaning or the example sentence: hints, imports, the inbox and the word list follow it.

asks.title: What does each card ask for?
asks.desc: When you type an answer or take a test, your answer is compared with this field. E.g. with “Meaning”, you aren't expected to type the example sentence and source shown on the back.

notetype.preview_desc: This is how the cards of this type look. As sample content, each field shows its own name.
notetype.preview_broken: The template code can't make cards like this, so it can't be saved:
notetype.save_loses_field: “{name}” will be removed: its content in {notes, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} is lost.
notetype.save_new_cards: The new “{name}” template adds a card to each of the {notes, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} of this type (unless its front would be empty).
notetype.delete_classic: Classic is the app's base type and can't be deleted. Other types you don't use can be.
notetype.delete_in_use: {notes, plural, one {# note uses} other {# notes use}} this type. A type with notes can't be deleted: first select those notes in the Library and move them with “Change note type”, or delete them.
notetype.delete_free: No note uses this type, so deleting it affects no notes or cards. Undo brings it back.
notetype.delete_subtitle: The Subtitle extension saves the words it captures as this type; if you delete it, no new cards arrive from the extension.
notetype.remove_field_body: When you save, the “{name}” content of {notes, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} is deleted. Their other fields, cards and review history stay as they are; Undo brings it back.
notetype.remove_template_body: No cards have been made from this template yet, so removing it affects no cards. Until you save, Discard brings it back.
notetype.switch_body: You haven't saved your changes to “{name}”. They are lost if you switch to another type.
notetype.field_used_body: This field is shown by the {templates} template. First take {code} out of the template under “Advanced: template code” below; then you can remove the field.
notetype.template_in_use_body: {cards, plural, one {# card was} other {# cards were}} made from this template (counting the trash). Removing a template with cards would leave those cards and their review history orphaned, so the app doesn't allow it. You can still edit its front and back code.

code.title: Advanced: template code
code.summary: The cards' HTML templates, CSS styling and the fields' technical settings. No need to open it unless you want to write the card design yourself.
code.fields_desc: Each field's kind (text, picture, sound…), the duplicate check and whether search looks inside it.
code.unique_hint: if all ticked fields match another note, the new note counts as a duplicate.
code.searchable_hint: search also looks inside this field.
code.codes_new: New fields get their code when you save.
code.css_desc: Styling applied only to the cards of this type.
code.new_template_cards: When you save, each of the {notes, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}} of this type gets a card from this template (unless its front would be empty).

start.intro: Pick a starting point and give it a name. You can change its fields and looks afterwards.
start.label: Starting point
start.missing: This ready-made type was deleted, so it can't be used.
start.name_hint: You see this name in the type list when adding a note.

word.title: Word
word.name: My words
word.desc: The word on the front, its meaning on the back. One card per word.

word_example.title: Word + example sentence
word_example.name: Word and example
word_example.desc: The word on the front; its meaning and a sentence using it on the back.

reverse.title: Both directions
reverse.name: Both ways
reverse.desc: Each note becomes 2 cards, front→back and back→front, so you're asked both ways.

cloze.title: Fill in the blank (cloze)
cloze.name: Fill in the blank
cloze.desc: Every word you hide in a sentence becomes its own card.

subtitle.title: Subtitle
subtitle.name: Subtitle words
subtitle.desc: The same fields as the Subtitle extension's cards: word, subtitle line, meaning, translation, screenshot. The extension keeps using its own ready-made type.

blank.title: Plain: front and back
blank.name: New note type
blank.desc: Two fields, one card. Start here if you want to shape it yourself.
